modelName: Offered is not delivered — the acceptance rule on a SODOTO teach pair
modelNote: Verna Allee's completion rule applied to SODOTO. A mentor can extend teaching indefinitely; nothing has converted until the learner accepts, and in SODOTO the badge IS the acceptance — signed, held in the learner's own site. This is the one notation rule that changes what our badge data means: five teaching sessions with no badges are five dangling offers, not five successes. Built 2026-08-31 with Marc Pierson. EVIDENCE: every arrow here is marked "asserted" because this file is an illustration. Drawn from the real badge ledger every arrow would be "observed" — a signed record rather than a self-report — which is the whole reason this method is stronger on SODOTO data than on anything else we hold. IAD LEVEL: collective-choice (asserted 2026-08-31, open to correction at the Ostrom Workshop). Spans. The teaching and demonstrating arrows are operational, but the badge is the mechanism assigning a participant to a new position — someone who may now teach this. Issuing it is a POSITION RULE operating, not an operational act, and that is what the file is actually about.

legendEntries.label: A person in a teaching pair
OFFERED AND NEVER CLOSED — not a success

nodes.label: Same mentor. Same skill. Four sessions. ONE completed transaction.
nodes.note: Everything above the mentor closed. Everything below it did not. Under the old reading this is a mentor who taught four people. Under Allee's rule it is a mentor with one conversion and three dead links — and the second reading is the one that tells you whether the capability actually moved.

nodes.label: MENTOR
nodes.note: Holds the skill and is willing to give it away. In value-network terms this role initiates a potential deliverable; it cannot complete the transaction on its own.

nodes.label: DOROTHY
nodes.note: Received the teaching, did it unassisted while the mentor watched, and now holds a signed badge in her own site under her own key. The transaction is complete and provable without asking anyone how they feel about it.

nodes.label: BADGE
nodes.note: Not a certificate and not a score. It is the acceptance stamp that converts an offer into a completed value transaction — and because it is signed and self-held, it is a transaction record rather than a self-report. This is precisely why Snowden's face-saving objection to social network data does not bite here: nobody was asked to describe a relationship.

nodes.label: LEARNER A
nodes.note: Sat through the session. Nodded. No badge. Nothing converted.

nodes.label: LEARNER B
nodes.note: Sat through the session. No badge. Nothing converted.

nodes.label: LEARNER C
nodes.note: Sat through the session. No badge. Nothing converted.

nodes.label: COMPLETED. Both halves offered, and the badge closed it. This one counts.
nodes.note: The pair of dashed arrows bows apart into the counterflow lens: teaching goes one way, demonstrated competence comes back the other. The badge sits on the pair and seals it.

nodes.label: THREE sessions happened. Zero transactions completed. Do not count these as teaching.
nodes.note: The failure this notation catches is a reporting failure, not a teaching failure. Somebody genuinely spent three afternoons doing this. What the drawing refuses to do is let three afternoons be reported as three people who now hold the skill — because nothing in the record says they do.

edges.label: shows: how to publish a FedWiki page
edges.note: The SEE and DO halves of SODOTO, offered.

edges.label: does it unassisted, witnessed
edges.note: The return deliverable. Demonstrated competence is itself a value output — the mentor learns whether the teaching worked.

edges.label: issues signed badge
edges.note: The mentor's attestation, signed in the browser by the mentor — never programmatically.

edges.label: accepted — held in her own site
edges.note: Acceptance is storage under her own key. That is what makes it hers rather than a record about her.

edges.label: shown — never closed
edges.note: A dead link in Allee's exchange analysis: value extended, never converted.
